name: 4965 Washington Street
headline: Evergreen Real Estate Group, Rocky Mountain Communities and the GES Coalition (as Globeville Redevelopment Partners) are building 4965 Washington Street, a five-story mass-timber building with 170 family apartments for households at 30% to 80% AMI above a new Denver Public Library branch, on city-owned land in Globeville. It won a 2025 federal 4% credit award from CHFA backed by Denver Housing Authority bonds.
why_it_matters: It stacks nearly every city tool on one site: land the city bought with CDBG and linkage fees and leases back for $10 a year for 99 years, a $9.8M HOST gap loan, 20 city-funded project-based vouchers, the city's bond cap delegated to DHA, and a $9.1M city purchase of the library condo at completion.

status.label: Under construction since January 2026; completion expected fall 2027
status.detail: National Equity Fund reported on 2026-01-26 that financing had closed and construction had started, with officials marking it earlier that month, and Naked Denver reported on 2026-03-19 that construction was underway. Completion is expected in fall 2027, with preleasing in summer 2027; the land lease requires substantial completion by 2027-11-30.

next_step: Watch for the city's closing on the library condominium unit (RISE bond money, agreement runs to 2027-12-31), a certificate of occupancy and summer 2027 preleasing.

key_numbers.value: 170 homes, all income-restricted, 85 of them at or below 50% AMI
key_numbers.meaning: 60 units at 30% AMI, 25 at 50%, 22 at 70% and 63 at 80%; half the homes have three or four bedrooms, and 20 are permanent supportive housing units.
About $57.5M over 10 years, with $57,700,000 of Denver Housing Authority private activity bonds per CHFA; no state credit.
News reports at groundbreaking say $132M; the city's March 2025 HUD notice estimated $123,131,808.

key_numbers.value: $9.8M city gap loan plus $22.6M in city voucher funding
key_numbers.meaning: A 20-year HOST loan ($4M must-pay, $5.8M paid from cash flow) and a 20-year, $22,550,681 contract for 20 city Homeless Resolution project-based vouchers.

facts.value: 4965 Washington Street, Denver 80216 (Globeville). The site combines 4995 Washington Street with 4964 N. Pearl Street and 624 E. 50th Street; earlier records use the 4995 Washington address
Family, new construction; in a QCT; not DDA or SADDA; Section 8 column marked No
About 3.2 acres, zoned G-MS-5, a former car dealership

Five stories, about 250,000 sq ft, prefabricated cross-laminated timber with a steel-frame facade, all-electric; described as the first affordable development in Colorado to use CLT as a major design component

A Denver Public Library branch of about 10,000 sq ft (Globeville's first permanent branch) and about 4,100 sq ft of community commercial space owned by the GES Coalition, planned as a cafe run by Tierra Colectiva
A small planned community of three condominium units: the housing (owner entity), the library (to be bought by the city) and the commercial space (GES Coalition)
4965 Washington Street LLLP, a Colorado limited liability limited partnership, an affiliate of Evergreen Real Estate Group and Rocky Mountain Communities
111 parking spaces, including EV charging, and about 50,000 sq ft of outdoor space
20 permanent supportive housing units for households at or below 30% AMI experiencing homelessness, with on-site services by Family Tree
City covenant runs with the land for at least 99 years; the land lease runs 99 years

background.text: Denver Council approved the purchase of 4995 Washington Street from TRE 4995 LLC for $6,000,000 in December 2018 (file 18-1414) for future housing and mixed-use development; the city paid for it with CDBG funds.

The city sought developers in January 2022, preferring a 99-year ground lease at a nominal $10 a year, and HOST and the Department of Finance picked Globeville Redevelopment Partners through an RFP in September 2022.

Council approved a site control and ground lease option agreement with Globeville Redevelopment Partners on 2022-10-24 (file 22-1270) and extended it to 2025-06-30 on 2025-03-17 (file 25-0259), adding two parcels bought in 2024.

In June 2024 Council approved buying 4964 N. Pearl Street and 624 E. 50th Street from Globeville Redevelopment Partners for $2,350,000 (file 24-0638) to enlarge the site and improve access; the city's 2025 briefing says linkage fees paid for them.
HOST issued a finding of no significant impact on 2025-03-20 and planned to ask HUD to release the CDBG money tied to the parcel; no new HUD money was attached to the project.

On 2025-09-08 Council passed four measures together: the $9.8M HOST loan, the 20-voucher contract, the $9.1M library purchase and the 99-year land lease, which is assigned to 4965 Washington Street LLLP at closing.
The land lease requires construction to start within 60 days of its effective date and substantial completion by 2027-11-30, unless the city's real estate director extends those dates.
The city's RFP terms required at least half the units to have three or four bedrooms and at least 35% of units at or below 30% AMI; the unit mix meets both.
The GES Coalition's ownership interest in the commercial unit is meant to allow below-market rent for a community cafe or market.

discrepancies.text: CHFA lists $57,700,000 of Denver Housing Authority bonds, while the DHA TEFRA notice allows up to $85,000,000 and Connect CRE reports $85 million in DHA revenue bonds.
HOST's March 2025 HUD notice estimates total project cost at $123,131,808, while 2026 news reports put it at $132 million.

The city's May 2025 briefing lists the ground lease rent restrictions as 50 units at 80% AMI and 35 at 70% AMI, while the unit table in the same briefing and CHFA show 63 at 80% AMI and 22 at 70% AMI.
The city's May 2025 briefing puts the library purchase at $9,000,000, while the resolution Council passed sets $9,100,000 and Naked Denver describes a $12 million RISE bond investment in the library.
Council approved buying the two added parcels for $2,350,000, while the city's 2025 briefing lists their prices as $850,000 and $1,300,000 ($2,150,000 together).
Naked Denver described eligible households as earning 30% to 60% of AMI, while the city, CHFA and other reports say 30% to 80%.

Naked Denver in October 2025 reported a groundbreaking ceremony scheduled for October 23, while National Equity Fund and REBusiness describe the closing and groundbreaking as taking place in January 2026.
